title: CI/CD rollback breadcrumbs — canary failure post-release
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal breadcrumbs for the canary rollback we executed on 2024-11-13. Writing this down while details are fresh so the postmortem can borrow commands/timestamps.

Incident summary (high level):
- Release: platform service v2024.11.13-rc3 (image tag: registry.redwood.ai/platform:v20241113-rc3)
- Deployment pattern: canary rollout (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) using rollout controller v0.9.2
- Problem: Within ~20 minutes of canary start, canary pods reported a high error rate (~20% 5xx on /generate endpoint) and increased tail latency. Observed request timeouts and retries from client side.
- Action taken: paused rollout at 25%, rolled back canary traffic to stable (v2024.11.11), scaled down canary pods, and rolled back image to last-known-good.

Timeline (approx):
- 11:02 UTC: Started canary rollout -> 10% traffic to v20241113-rc3 (controller: rollout-controller-0.9.2).
- 11:08 UTC: Observed tail-latency increase in Datadog p95 from 120ms -> 480ms for canary pods.
- 11:10 UTC: 5xx rate on /generate spiked to ~18% (canary).
- 11:12 UTC: Alerts fired (pager duty: infra-release).
- 11:15 UTC: Paused rollout at 25% (manual via kubectl rollout pause). Began investigation.
- 11:20 UTC: Executed rollback to stable image and removed canary label for traffic routing.
- 11:32 UTC: Verified error rates returned to baseline for stable.

Commands and snippets used (breadcrumbs):
- To check rollout status: 
  kubectl -n platform rollout status rollout/platform-service-rollout -w
  # output: Waiting for canary replicaSets to finish...

- To inspect pods and images: 
  kubectl -n platform get pods -l rollout=platform-service-rollout -o wide
  # observed pods: platform-canary-xxxx  Image: registry.redwood.ai/platform:v20241113-rc3

- To tail logs from a canary pod (captured useful error snippet below):
  kubectl -n platform logs -f platform-canary-abcde -c platform

- To pause rollout: 
  kubectl -n platform annotate rollout/platform-service-rollout staged-rollout=true --overwrite
  kubectl -n platform rollout pause rollout/platform-service-rollout
  # confirmed with: kubectl -n platform get rollout platform-service-rollout -o yaml | grep paused: true

- To patch traffic routing back to stable service (service split):
  # our router uses service weights stored in ConfigMap: platform/traffic-split-config
  kubectl -n platform get configmap traffic-split-config -o yaml > /tmp/traffic.yaml
  # edit weights: set canary: 0, stable: 100
  kubectl -n platform apply -f /tmp/traffic.yaml
  # validated via: curl -sS -H "x-request-id: debug" https://canary-check.internal/generate | grep "v20241111"

- To scale down canary deployment quickly: 
  kubectl -n platform scale deployment platform-canary --replicas=0

- To rollback deployment image to last-known-good (explicit set): 
  kubectl -n platform set image deployment/platform-stable platform=registry.redwood.ai/platform:v20241111
  kubectl -n platform rollout status deployment/platform-stable -w

Error snippets found in canary logs (raw examples):
- 2024-11-13T11:06:34Z ERROR runtime request_handler: "upstream request failed: HTTP 524: origin timed out" (repeated, different traces)
- 2024-11-13T11:07:02Z WARN model-serving latency:  p95=486ms  p99=1.2s  -> observed request queue depth spike
- 2024-11-13T11:09:01Z ERROR kv-cache: Failed to load prefix cache entry id=0x23fa: io timeout

Hypotheses (initial):
- Hypothesis A: New image introduced a regression in model-serving path that caused slower I/O to KV cache under certain sequence-length distributions. Evidence: kv-cache timeouts in logs, latency climb correlated with requests size distribution shift during canary window.
- Hypothesis B: Kernel/QoS with new CUDA driver collisions (less likely but possible in Dedicated pools). We saw one canary host with slightly different driver (node-provisioning drift).
- Hypothesis C: Load shaping change in canary traffic (edge routed slightly different path) exposing network/disk hot-spot.

What we tried (quick list):
- Rollback image -> stable (result: restored baseline).
- Scaled canary pods to 0 and re-routed traffic (result: baseline restored).
- Pulled logs from canary pods and compared to stable -> kv-cache errors only present on canary.
- Ran a single-node repro load (locust) against canary image in staging with long sequences -> reproduced increased io timeouts.

Reproduction notes (staging):
- Reproducer steps:
  1) Deploy image v20241113-rc3 to staging with same config as production (env, kv cache endpoint).
  2) Run load generator with request distribution: 20% > 1k tokens, 80% 128 tokens.
  3) Observe p95 and kv-cache error rates.
- Observed same kv-cache timeouts in staging after ~90s of traffic.

Artifact/versioning notes (important for postmortem):
- Image tags: registry.redwood.ai/platform:v20241111 (stable), v20241113-rc3 (canary/problem), v20241113-rc2 (previous rc).
- SHA of failing image: sha256:abcdef1234567890deadbeef (from registry)
- Build metadata: buildkite pipeline #2304, commit: 1a2b3c4d (PR: #987).

Immediate next steps I recorded in channel at 11:25 UTC:
- Create INFRA ticket with timeline and attach logs (INFRA-1423).
- Reproduce in staging with extra debug flags (kv-cache verbose).
- Re-run canary only after root cause identified or patch cut.

Longer-term follow-up items (for postmortem / release engineering):
- Add preflight load test for long-sequence tail latency against kv-cache endpoints for every release.
- Add a rollout health check that includes kv-cache error rate threshold (not just p95).
- Hard pin node image/driver versions for Dedicated pools used by canaries or add compatibility test in CI.
- Improve rollout rollback automation to instantly revert traffic weights if kv-cache errors exceed threshold for >2 minutes.

Notes to self / things to verify before writing postmortem:
- Pull full pod logs from all affected canary nodes and attach corresponding node driver/kernel versions (kubectl describe node).
- Check registry build logs for any changes in cache initialization code between rc2 and rc3 (grep for kv-cache init changes).
- Confirm whether any infra changes (e.g., kubelet upgrades, node reprovisioning) happened in the 24h window prior to release.

Slack snippets I posted (for record):
- "Paused rollout at 25% — seeing kv-cache io timeouts and p95 spike. Rolling back to v20241111 and scaling canary to 0. Investigating logs now. INFRA-1423 created."

Known follow-ups assigned: 
- Priya -> reproduce in staging and collect flamegraphs for v20241113-rc3 (deadline: 2024-11-15)
- Ethan -> check node driver/kernel diffs across canary hosts and stable hosts (deadline: 2024-11-15)
- Alex (me) -> write postmortem draft and propose rollout guard changes (deadline: 2024-11-18)

Bottom line (quick takeaway):
- Rollback was appropriate and restored baseline quickly. Initial evidence points to an application-level regression that causes kv-cache timeouts under heavy long-sequence load, not a pure infra network failure. Need staged repro + root cause fix before trying rc3 again.

Attachments to include in postmortem (links):
- Datadog dashboard snapshots (time-range 2024-11-13T11:00-11:40)
- Pod logs tarball: s3://redwood-incidental-logs/infra-1423/pod-logs.tar.gz
- Build metadata: https://buildkite.com/redwood/platform/builds/2304

End of breadcrumbs. Will convert these notes into the initial postmortem doc and link PRs when done.
